name: Cerebellar Circuits, Deep Nuclei and Ataxia

reference.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students / Snell's Clinical Neuroanatomy
clinicalPearls: Deep cerebellar nuclei from lateral to medial: Dentate, Emboliform, Globose, Fastigial (Don't Eat Greasy Food)
Purkinje cells provide the sole output from the cerebellar cortex, releasing inhibitory GABA onto deep nuclei
Climbing fibres arise exclusively from inferior olivary nucleus, making multiple synapses directly on Purkinje cells (error signaling)
Mossy fibres originate from pontine nuclei and spinal cord, synapsing on granule cells whose parallel fibres excite Purkinje cells
Cerebellar lesions produce ipsilateral deficits: vermis lesions cause truncal ataxia; hemispheric lesions cause intention tremor and dysmetria
reference.pathophysiology: The cerebellum functions as a motor comparator, adjusting movement trajectories by comparing intended motor commands from cerebral cortex with proprioceptive feedback from periphery. Vermian lesions disrupt vestibular and axial balance. Hemispheric damage impairs rapid alternating movements (dysdiadochokinesia) and terminal targeting (past-pointing, intention tremor).
additionalDifferentials: Multiple system atrophy cerebellar type (MSA-C, hot cross bun sign)
additionalInvestigations: MRI brain with sagittal T1 and axial FLAIR sequences for cerebellar atrophy or mass
Genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxias (SCA trinucleotide repeats)
Screening for paraneoplastic anti-Yo / anti-Hu antibodies
